- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show strong upward bias after recent price spikes; model fails to correct for sharp declines following peaks.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — overcorrects downward after high peaks, then undercorrects as prices rebound.
- Forecast trend often lags true price movement by 1–3 days, particularly in downward corrections.
- Model underestimates volatility in mid-to-late forecast horizon; fails to capture sudden drops or sharp rebounds.
- Forecasts tend to be smoother than true price series, missing short-term noise and structural breaks.
- Model overfits recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation in subsequent days.
- Forecasts show diminishing sensitivity to recent data as horizon extends — model becomes less responsive to recent spikes.
